paraphrase: When touched by painful bodily feeling the uninstructed person sorrows and laments and so feels two feelings, bodily and mental, as if struck by a dart and then by a second dart; resisting the pain he seeks sensual pleasure as the only escape he knows, and the tendencies to aversion, lust and ignorance lie within him.

paraphrase: The instructed noble disciple feels only one feeling, bodily, not mental — struck by one dart only; he does not resist it, knows an escape other than sensual pleasure, understands the origin, passing, gratification, danger and escape of feelings, and feels them detached: he is called one detached from birth, ageing and death.
